key_headlines.title: Korean Current Account Balance Hits Record High Boosted by Semiconductors
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's GDP growth forecast averaged 3.7%, up 0.2 percentage points from a month prior, representing seven consecutive months of upward revisions driven by strong semiconductor exports.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's stock market experienced significant volatility following US midterm elections, with KOSPI dropping 5.28% and semiconductor giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix falling sharply. The market weakness reflects global concerns about AI investment sustainability and potential US policy shifts. However, government officials and semiconductor experts maintain that long-term growth prospects remain solid due to continued big tech investments and expanding AI agent adoption. Domestic companies are expanding long-term supply contracts while closely monitoring policy uncertainties following the US elections.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: South Korea's GDP growth forecast has been raised to an average of 3.7%, marking the seventh consecutive monthly upward revision, primarily driven by strong semiconductor sector performance. The country's current account balance reached a record high, demonstrating the positive economic impact of semiconductor exports. Meanwhile, US employment data surprised positively with 165,000 jobs added in October and unemployment falling to 4.1%, strengthening the case for potential Federal Reserve rate increases in December despite inflation remaining above the 2% target.
sections.Financial Markets: KOSPI and KOSDAQ opened weak with semiconductor stocks showing mixed performance, while the Korean won-dollar exchange rate stood at 1,360.7 won. Samsung Asset Management launched a new ETF combining US short-term Treasury bonds and Nasdaq-100 index with monthly dividends. Market analysts warn of extreme oversold conditions in KOSPI and recommend maintaining cash positions, though strong US employment data provided some support for recovery potential in global markets.
sections.Industry & Technology: Middle East tensions creating energy inflation have become a tailwind for Korean EV exports to Europe, particularly benefiting Hyundai and Kia. Korean equipment companies are expanding into new sectors, with laser processing specialist HK securing orders for next-generation automotive production lines and AI Korea receiving semiconductor cluster equipment contracts in Yongin. Multiple Korean firms are diversifying their industrial portfolios and strengthening supply chain positions across semiconductors, batteries, and automotive sectors.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's villa (multi-unit housing) lease market shows record low inventory for Q1 next year with less than 20,000 units available, as aftermath of jeonse fraud cases reduces new supply while rental prices rise. Reconstruction excess profit recovery system is now materializing, with properties in Daechi-dong facing average additional burden fees of 4.6 billion won. Gyeonggi Province faces financial difficulties and is considering selling its Gwanggyo new provincial office building just 4.5 years after occupancy, while Seoul property prices continue appreciating significantly.
sections.International Economy: Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress plan to eliminate Trump's tariff policies, targeting Canadian goods first while seeking to return tariff authority from the president to Congress. US Fed officials signal potential rate hikes in December based on strong employment data, despite concerns about rising costs without additional fiscal resources. Korean companies are actively participating in global biotech and AI partnerships, with S Biometrics attending Europe's largest biotech conference and IL joining the EU's AI, Data and Robotics Association.
sections.AI & Economy: AI is reshaping global advertising markets, with Meta's ad revenue growing 26% compared to Google's 12% growth, demonstrating AI's differential impact on tech giants. US Democrat plans to regulate AI data center construction through permitting and power restrictions create potential opportunities for Korea to attract investments. Seoul city is implementing AI administrative innovations based on employee ideas for nighttime economy activation, while companies like S-Net Systems are leveraging renewable energy infrastructure expertise to enter AI data center markets.
sections.Others: US midterm election outcome raises concerns about stability of Korea-US alliance and joint security projects under Trump administration. KB Asset Management continues its RISE Hero Store social contribution program for bereaved families of fallen firefighters with 20 million won donation. Korean Package secured exclusive 5-year supply contract for sterile packaging with Chinese Lamipak to expand product portfolio, while political attention shifts to 2028 US presidential race as Democratic candidates gain prominence.
